name: mean_reversion_hull_ma
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, during mid-session ranging periods (flat HMA slope), the Hull Moving Average over 3 minutes (36 × 5s bars) serves as a real-time equilibrium anchor because its lag-less construction tracks where sustained institutional order flow has been placed. When NIFTY deviates >0.12% (≈25-27 spot points) from this HMA while the slope is near-zero, VWAP-benchmarked execution algos and market makers see the index as statistically cheap or expensive relative to recent flow — their delta-hedging and mean-reversion fills push price back toward the HMA within 30-90 seconds. The flat-slope filter is critical: it rules out trending regimes where the overshoot is justified by sustained directional order flow, isolating only the pure microstructure overshoots.

indicators.name: hma_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute Hull Moving Average. Original used 50-min HMA on 1-min bars (50-min equilibrium, 10-40 min hold). We compress to 3-min because our hold is 15-90s — the mean-reversion trigger and the equilibrium anchor must be at the same timescale. A 50-min HMA is too slow to flag micro-overshoots that resolve in under 2 minutes. HMA chosen over EMA/SMA because its lag-less property means it already reflects where the market settled 2-3 minutes ago, not a smoothed lag of historical data.

indicators.name: dist_hma
indicators.purpose: Signed fractional deviation from HMA. Threshold at 0.12% (≈26 pts on NIFTY at 22000) — large enough to represent a genuine microstructure overshoot beyond normal 5s noise (~2-4 pts), small enough that 50% reversion is achievable in 30-90 seconds.

indicators.name: hma_slope_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute HMA slope (change over 12 bars = 60 seconds). Threshold < 0.03% per minute identifies flat regime. This is the key filter: if HMA is sloping, the deviation is justified by trend and reversion thesis fails. 12-bar window chosen because it matches the time stop (we want slope context over the same timescale as our hold period).

conditions: abs(hma_slope_12) < slope_threshold (HMA flat — no persistent trend)
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions must be true simultaneously on same 5s bar

conditions: abs(hma_slope_12) < slope_threshold (HMA flat — no persistent trend)
buy_pe.confirmation: All conditions must be true simultaneously on same 5s bar

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts = 6 NIFTY spot pts additional adverse move. At 0.12% initial deviation (≈26 pts), if NIFTY extends another 6 pts in the same direction, total deviation exceeds 32 pts and the flat-HMA regime assumption has broken — a trend has begun. This is the narrowest stop justified: a 30-60 second non-reverting overshoot on a flat-HMA NIFTY typically signals regime change, not deeper mean reversion.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option pts ≈ 12 NIFTY spot pts of reversion. From a 26-pt overshoot, recovering 12 pts (≈46%) is the conservative estimate — NIFTY typically recovers 50-70% of a ranging overshoot within 60-90 seconds when HMA is genuinely flat. Targeting 12 pts rather than full reversion (26 pts) gives a high probability of completion within the 90s time stop. R:R = 1:2.

filters.vix_filter: none — HMA flatness filter already excludes high-volatility trending regimes
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; skip first 15 minutes of session to avoid opening-range spikes that look like deviations but are information absorption
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY volume at 5s is noisy; HMA slope filter is a cleaner proxy for regime
filters.trend_filter: embedded — hma_slope_12 < slope_threshold is the trend filter

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — as more algorithms run HMA mean reversion, overshoots resolve faster and the edge compresses; but the flat-slope filter provides some durability by only trading genuine ranging regimes

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from original: (1) Lookback compressed from 50-min to 3-min (36 bars) to match the 15-90s hold time — original's 10-40 min hold scales to 1-7 min at 5s, and we use the lower end. (2) Deviation threshold lowered from 1% to 0.12% — NIFTY index is smoother than individual F&O stocks; 1% would be a ~220pt deviation that is rare and takes 10+ minutes to revert, not our target timescale. (3) Slope threshold introduced as absolute % rather than binary HMA[0]>HMA[1] — 5-second HMA is noisy and a single bar up/down comparison is unreliable; use 12-bar slope to confirm flat regime. Session shifted to start at 09:30 (vs original 10:30) because NIFTY mid-session ranging can begin from 09:30 once the opening drive completes.
weaknesses: HMA slope filter can over-exclude: in strongly trending sessions, almost no trades fire, creating zero-trade days
0.12% threshold on NIFTY triggers more frequently during high-VIX days when mean reversion is less reliable
WMA computation is O(n * period) — 36-bar HMA on full session of 3375 bars is ~120k operations, acceptable but not trivial
Original thesis ('behavioral bias: traders chase') is harder to argue at index level — institutional flow dominates, so the mechanism is more microstructure-based than behavioral
